title: Synthesis and Tribological Characteristics of High-Performance Self-Lubricating CoCrFeNiMo<sub>x</sub>-Ni/MoS<sub>2</sub>-Ag-Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> Composites.

recollection.starting_material: CoCrFeNiMo_x high-entropy alloy powders (fcc HEA) combined with Ni-coated MoS2 (Ni/MoS2) solid lubricant powder, elemental Ag powder, and Cr2O3 ceramic reinforcement; HEA powder prepared by gas atomization or mechanical alloying; MoS2 particles Ni-plated to improve thermal stability and interfacial bonding.
recollection.intervention: Powder blending and consolidation by spark plasma sintering (or hot pressing) to near-full density; systematic variation of Mo content x in the HEA matrix and of Ni/MoS2–Ag–Cr2O3 loadings; tribological testing in dry sliding from room temperature to 600 C (typ. 5–10 N load, ~0.2 m/s) against a ceramic counterbody (e.g., Al2O3 or Si3N4) to assess friction and wear; microstructural/chemical analyses of worn surfaces and cross-sections.
recollection.structure: A dense fcc CoCrFeNiMo_x matrix with uniformly dispersed Ag and Cr2O3 particles; Ni-coated MoS2 retained as discrete lamellae with improved interfacial bonding; limited secondary phases from Mo addition (avoiding excessive brittle sigma at optimized x); during sliding a continuous tribo-film forms comprising MoS2/Ag and oxides (Cr2O3 and (Fe,Co,Ni) spinels) with possible Ag–Mo–O phases.
recollection.mechanism: At room temperature, low shear is governed by MoS2 basal-plane sliding, aided by smearing Ag that bridges cracks and fills asperities; the Ni shell on MoS2 suppresses sulfidation/decomposition during sintering and enhances load transfer. At elevated temperatures, partial oxidation of MoS2 to MoO3 and interaction with Ag produces lubricious Ag2MoO4/Ag–Mo–O phases; concurrently, Cr2O3 and HEA-derived spinel oxides form a hard, adherent glaze that anchors the lubricants and reduces ploughing. The combination yields a robust, self-replenishing tribo-film spanning RT–600 C.
recollection.results: Guess: The optimized composite (e.g., x≈0.2–0.3 in HEA; ~5–10 wt% Ni/MoS2, ~5 wt% Ag, ~5 wt% Cr2O3) achieved near-full density (98–99%) and hardness on the order of 5–7 GPa. Under 5 N and ~0.2 m/s at RT, the friction coefficient dropped to ~0.15±0.03 with a wear rate ~1–3×10^-6 mm^3/N·m. From 300 to 600 C, friction remained low (~0.20–0.28) with wear rates ~1×10^-6–5×10^-6 mm^3/N·m due to a continuous Ag–Mo–O/spinel glaze. A baseline HEA or composites without lubricants showed μ~0.55–0.7 and wear rates one to two orders of magnitude higher; replacing Ni/MoS2 with bare MoS2 increased μ and wear, indicating the Ni coating’s benefit. The composite exhibited stable performance over long sliding distances with minimal counterface damage.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies Mo-content variation, powder consolidation, an FCC matrix with Mo-related secondary phases, and temperature-dependent MoS2/Ag versus oxide/silver-molybdate tribofilms. However, it incorrectly claims that lubricant/reinforcement loadings were varied, truncates testing at 600 °C, mischaracterizes optimization and sigma-phase behavior, and invents comparisons with baseline or bare-MoS2 materials. Its numerical composition, hardness, friction, wear, and optimal-x estimates do not match the reported values.
